question: Can the 1596 Datong worked example's dynamic truncation widths be generalized into a source-certified runtime precision policy?

evidence_layers.finding: Direct primary ledgers require different fixed-point operators by table-generation stage; this disproves one global rounding helper but does not define dynamic event-interpolation precision.
The printed example truncates the within-limit Chi difference to six decimal degree places and the D1 add-correction to two decimal source units.

The peer-reviewed 1527 reconstruction supports recoverability of Datong qishuo/date computation, while the later explicit comparison study notes that the 2011 paper did not compare Ming almanac conjunction times.

findings.narrowest_control: 1639 month 4, 巳正四刻, about 2.304 minutes full width by the published decimal-bin representation

evidence_layers.source_boundary: The comparison exposes final D1/D2 times and printed almanac bins, not Ming intermediate Chi-difference/division residues.

evidence_layers.finding: The 13/13 day-level replay and physical 12/12 month-page chain remain valid, but its day-boundary margins cannot select a sub-stage dynamic rounding profile.
The same Ming author prints different intermediate widths in a Shoushi example. It is not Datong production authority and forbids author-wide/context-free fixed-width inference.
Later exegesis supports stage-scoped collect-up versus discard semantics in table construction but does not close Ming dynamic D1 event-computation precision.

adjudication.reason: Final-output time-bin agreement constrains the complete D1 calculation but does not uniquely identify which intermediate truncation/carry profile produced those outputs.

precision_profile_experiment_contract.required_output: Replay all 56 final conjunction bins and identify whether printed observations discriminate profiles; numerical fit alone does not establish historical authority.

next_research_priority.focus: Build a research-only precision-profile sensitivity harness over the 56 conjunction-time bins; keep G05 open unless evidence both discriminates profiles and supports a historically bounded rule.
